name: Land acquisition closing and due diligence
summary: Buyer-side costs of acquiring land: owner's title insurance, escrow/recording, any buyer-paid share of transfer taxes, and pre-closing due diligence. Transfer taxes dominate the spread: zero in some states, about 1% in Pennsylvania (plus local), 0.70% in Florida, and graduated up to 3% plus local in Washington. Who pays the transfer tax varies by state custom and contract, so the default assumes a partial buyer share. Broker commissions are excluded (usually seller-paid).

items.name: Land closing costs (buyer side)

range.method: Build-up: owner's title premium ~0.4%-0.8% of price at $100k-$10M (Texas promulgated rates, e1) + escrow, recording and closing ~0.2%-0.5% (judgment) + buyer share of transfer tax 0%-3% (PA 1% state, PHFA recognizes only half as a buyer cost, e3/e5; FL 0.70%, e4; WA graduated 1.1%-3% state, e2). Low ~1% (no transfer tax, title + escrow); mid 2% (title + escrow + ~1% transfer tax); high 4.5% (high-REET state plus local tax).

items.notes: Excludes broker commissions, land loan fees and mortgage recording taxes (see soft-costs titleClosingRecording) and any prorated property taxes.

items.name: Owner's title insurance premium

range.method: Texas promulgated basic premium: $780 on $100k (0.78%), $5,226 on $1M (0.52%), $21,466 on $5M (0.43%), $38,216 on $10M (0.38%) (e1). Mid 0.5% for a ~$1M-$3M land purchase. Other states' filed rates differ; Texas is one of the few with a single promulgated rate.

items.notes: Included inside landClosingCosts; listed separately for transparency.

items.name: Real estate transfer tax (state; local add-ons extra)

range.method: Low 0 for states with no state-level deed transfer tax (not individually verified in this session — check the state). Pennsylvania state rate 1% (e3); Florida $0.70 per $100 = 0.70% outside Miami-Dade (e4); Washington graduated state REET 1.10% up to $525k, 1.28%, 2.75%, 3.0% above $3.025M, plus local REET (e2). Mid 1% = typical of the taxing states sampled; high 3% = WA top bracket.

items.notes: Text guidance: transfer taxes are set by state and often by county/city on top (PA localities commonly add their own; Miami-Dade has a surtax on non-single-family transfers). Customary payer (buyer vs seller) varies; PHFA budgets only half as a buyer cost. Replace with the actual local rate whenever the location is known.

items.name: Land due diligence (pre-closing)

range.method: No public price source fetched. Built up by judgment for a 2-20 acre site: ALTA/topo survey $5k-$25k, Phase I ESA $2k-$6k, preliminary geotech $5k-$20k, zoning/entitlement and title review $2k-$15k, appraisal $3k-$10k, utility/wetland/traffic screening $0-$25k. Overlaps soft-costs thirdPartyReports and civilSurveyGeotech — the engine should not count the same report twice.

items.notes: Excludes Phase II ESA, wetland delineation/permits and traffic impact studies, which can each run five figures.

evidence.scopeNotes: Promulgated basic premium; value = $1M policy, low = $100k policy, high = $10M policy. Percent of coverage falls with amount.
State portion only; local REET is added. Thresholds rise on Jan. 1, 2027.

evidence.quote: imposed at a rate of 1 percent on the value of real estate
evidence.scopeNotes: State rate; local realty transfer taxes are collected in addition.

evidence.quote: 70 cents on each $100 or portion thereof of the total consideration.
evidence.scopeNotes: Deeds outside Miami-Dade; Miami-Dade 60 cents per $100 plus a 45-cent surtax on transfers other than single-family dwellings.

source.title: PHFA 2025 Underwriting Application — Development Cost Limits (revised 1-17-25)

evidence.quote: The Agency will only recognize one half of the transfer tax in the budget. The other half is the responsibility of the seller.
evidence.scopeNotes: Supports a partial buyer share of transfer tax in the default.
